citation: Jacob, R., Hill, H., & Corey, D. (2017). The impact of a professional development program on teachers' mathematical knowledge for teaching, instruction, and student achievement. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 10(2), 379-407. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2016.1273411
report_number: Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness 10(2):379-407
design: RCT; teacher/classroom-level random assignment WITHIN schools; 105 grade 4-5 teachers (51 treatment, 54 control) in 19 low-income schools in a single US district; subject = mathematics; 3-year 'Math Solutions' commercial PD (week-long summer institute each summer Aug 2010-Aug 2012 + 4-6 in-service days/year, >40 contact hrs/yr over 3 years) vs business-as-usual control (control teachers offered unrelated district science PD as incentive). Each year teachers taught a new set of students. Student impacts estimated via 2-level HLM (students nested in classrooms) with school fixed effects and pretest/demographic covariates.
problems: ROWS 52 AND 53 ARE THE SAME STUDY (confirmed duplicate). This single Jacob, Hill & Corey (2017) Math Solutions math-PD RCT was entered twice in the registry. All extracted student-math-achievement effect sizes are recorded ONCE under row_id 52; jacob_2017_r53 is intentionally left EMPTY (no effect_sizes carry row_id 53) to avoid double-counting in the central merge. SIGN DISCREPANCY: Table 8 reports State-Assessment Grade-5 at T4 (Year 3) as beta = -4.18 (favors control) but lists ES = +0.06; every other cell in Table 8 preserves the sign of beta (e.g. T2 State Grade 5 beta=-2.01/ES=-0.02), so the +0.06 is treated as a typo and the signed g is recorded as -0.06 (favoring control). Per-arm and per-grade student n at T4 are not broken out in the report (Table 8 gives only totals: T4 n=963 students, 56 classrooms); n_t/n_c are approximated from the 51:54 teacher split only to apply the negligible J correction. g_var/g_se are derived by propagating the HLM-based (cluster-adjusted) SE of beta onto the standardized scale (g_se = SE * |ES/beta| = SE / SD_pool), which is preferable to a naive student-level variance because the model accounts for clustering. Standardizing SD inferred from beta/ES per grade and test. The state test changed format/content between Year 1 and Years 2-3 but this does not affect the T4 impact estimate. All four T4 contrasts are null and non-significant, consistent with the paper's conclusion of no effect on student achievement.

effect_sizes.timepoint: post (T4 = spring of Year 3, end of 3-year treatment)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported Cohen's d (ES) from Table 8 = beta/SD_pool; g = J*d with J=0.998 (approx grade N~480) ~ unchanged at 2 dp. g_se from propagating HLM cluster-adjusted SE of beta to standardized scale: g_se = SE*|ES/beta| = 1.16*0.03/0.41 = 0.085; g_var = g_se^2. Standardized by within-grade student-level SD (~13.7).
